items.name: market-research
items.description: Use for market sizing (TAM, SAM, SOM both top-down and bottom-up), survey sample sizes or segment scoring. Runs market_sizer.py, sample_size_planner.py and segmentation_scorer.py and never returns one unsourced number.

items.name: product-research
items.description: Use when planning or synthesizing user research: choosing the method, deciding how many participants, or turning coded notes into insights. Runs study_designer.py, saturation_planner.py and insight_synthesizer.py, which refuses single-source insights.

items.name: research-finance
items.description: Use for R&D program money: multi-period budgets with indirect cost split, burn and runway against milestones, or capitalize vs expense routing. Runs program_budget_planner.py, burn_runway_tracker.py and capex_vs_opex_router.py.

items.name: research-ops-skills
items.description: Use when an enterprise research request needs routing (clinical study design, R&D finance, market sizing, user research): 'what sample size', 'R&D budget'. Lists the research-ops skills and routes to one.

items.name: deepread
items.description: Use when the user asks to deeply read a book, article, PDF, or document set; extract claims and evidence; build a knowledge map; or learn through Feynman explanation and recall. Covers quick, deep, map, Feynman, and whole-book reading modes.

items.name: dossier
items.description: Use for diligence or meeting prep on a specific company, person or organization ('prep me for a meeting with X', 'due diligence on Y'). Tests the user's stated hypothesis with balanced evidence (disconfirming_evidence_balance.py) and writes a .docx dossier.

items.name: grants
items.description: Use for any NIH funding question ('find grants for my research', 'which NIH institute'). Maps the idea to institutes, study sections and NOSIs via RePORTER, matches mechanisms with mechanism_matcher.py and writes a .docx strategy. NIH only.

items.name: litreview
items.description: Use when starting a literature review or a literature-based project. Plans the search (PICO, SPIDER) with framework_recommender.py, searches PubMed and OpenAlex with free_search.py and writes a .docx orientation guide. Single-paper lookups: query directly.

items.name: meta-research
items.description: Use when a wrong answer is expensive: strategy research, comparing several products or markets, validating a hypothesis with outside data. Fans out searches and sub-agents, triangulates each claim across 3+ sources and saves every source with quotes. Quick facts: answer directly.

items.name: notebooklm

items.name: patent

items.name: pulse
items.description: Use for what people are saying right now about a topic (trends, sentiment, complaints, tool comparisons) across Reddit, Hacker News and the web in a recent window. Returns a cited briefing with engagement signals.

items.name: syllabus
items.description: Use when the user shares a course syllabus or outline and wants supplementary readings. Groups topics with topic_grouper.py, finds recent peer-reviewed papers and writes a .docx with summaries and discussion questions.
